THE HEADLINES :-

 

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, India must innovate and lead the world in shaping technologies of tomorrow; Inaugurates Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 in New Delhi.

 

  1. BRICS Member Nations express deep concern over continued escalation of tensions in West Asia; Condemn any act of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable.

 

  1. Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Puducherry, Telangana and Chhattisgarh step up preparations as Cyclone Arnab advances towards east coast; Home Ministry directs state governments to take precautionary measures.

 

  1. India and Liechtenstein explore ways to boost ties in trade, investment and science and technology.

 

  1. In Sports, Aditya becomes U-19 World Boxing Champion in 55kg category.

 

  1. In Men’s Cricket, India beat hosts New Zealand by six wickets in third T-20 International at Wellington; Take three-nil lead in five-match series.

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow. After inaugurating the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Modi said India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly and lead the world in creating them. He stressed that a Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. Mr Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies.

 

Prime Minister Modi visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with people. The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors.

 

The three-day Conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities.

 

<><><>

 

BRICS Member Nations have expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation. In the Joint Declaration which was unanimously adopted today at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum held in New Delhi, the member countries urged to ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. The BRICS member countries said they encourage increasing efforts, through dialogue and diplomacy, towards a long-term understanding that will contribute to lasting peace, security and stability in the region.

 

“BRICS nations have stressed on the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law. They have condemned the imposition of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law. The member nations highlighted the importance of the Global South as a driver for positive change. They reaffirmed the role of BRICS in voicing its concerns and priorities. BRICS nations expressed strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable. They condemned the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22nd of April last year in the strongest terms. BRICS nations have urged to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism. WITH ANAND KUMAR, SUPARNA SAIKIA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

 

{{<><><>}}

 

Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Puducherry, Telangana and Chhattisgarh have stepped up preparations as Cyclone Arnab has advanced towards the eastern coast. Cyclone Arnab will hit Bapatla and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm tomorrow forenoon. Talking exclusively to Akashvani, Director General of India Meteorological Department (IMD) Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said that during landfall the cyclone will have maximum sustained wind speed upto 125 to 150 kilometres per hour. Dr. Mohapatra has cautioned people of destructive winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding.

 

Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh tomorrow.

 

The Ministry of Home Affairs has directed State Governments to keep a close watch, monitor the situation in their areas regularly and take appropriate precautionary measures in view of Cyclone Arnab. In an advisory, the Ministry has suggested for evacuating the people living in coastal areas to safer places and complete suspension of fishing operations.

 

In Andhra Pradesh, state authorities have stepped up preparedness as heavy to extremely heavy rainfall and coastal inundation are expected in several areas.

 

“The cyclone was centred 170 kilometres south-southeast of Visakhapatnam this evening. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is occurring in several districts, including Konaseema, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli, with isolated places likely to receive 21 centimetres or more of rainfall. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, while district administrations have established control rooms and intensified preparedness and relief measures. The State Disaster Management Authority has warned of seawater surges in vulnerable coastal areas and urged fishermen and residents of low-lying areas to remain alert. Meanwhile, more than 53 trains have been cancelled today and tomorrow as a precautionary measure. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

In Odisha, the state government has mobilised disaster-response teams and placed vulnerable districts on high alert. Rail services face widespread disruption, fishing operations have been suspended, and educational institutions in several districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after tomorrow.

 

“Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab’s pre-landfall process has started with rains in south and coastal Odisha, as the powerful weather system moves closer to the eastern coastline. According to the latest available India Meteorological Department bulletin, Arnab is about 380 kilometres south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha. Even as Odisha is on high alert, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has deployed eight ministers to oversee preparedness in vulnerable districts likely to be badly affected, while rescue teams, evacuation arrangements and relief shelters have been readied. Red warnings cover vulnerable southern districts, with heavy to extremely heavy rainfall threatening low-lying areas, roads, power lines and standing crops; more than 60 train services have been cancelled across the affected network and other services modified. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. The administration is racing against time to minimise damage and ensure public safety. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

<><><> 

 

Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan today said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He made these remarks while addressing the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture virtually at Akashvani Bhawan in New Delhi. Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate the 565 princely states together remains a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasized that Sardar Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the idea of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat.  

 

Mr Chouhan said that inspired by Sardar Patel’s policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, the country has responded firmly to threats from foreign forces and terrorists through various measures such as surgical strikes.

 

As a mark of respect to Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel, who was India’s first Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani hosts the annual Sardar Patel Memorial lecture. The recording of this lecture will be broadcast at 9:30 PM on the entire network of Akashvani on the occasion of Sardar Patel’s Birth Anniversary on 31st October.

 

{{<><><>}}

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Hereditary Prince of Liechtenstein, Alois today reaffirmed their commitment to working together to reform and strengthen multilateral institutions, including the United Nations. The Ministry of External Affairs said that they held extensive discussions today and reviewed the entire spectrum of India and Liechtenstein relations. The two leaders discussed ways to further deepen cooperation in key areas, including trade and investment, innovation, science and technology, skill development and people-to-people ties. They welcomed the positive momentum generated by the India-EFTA TEPA and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the bilateral partnership. India and Liechtenstein discussed proposal for Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between the two countries. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, Secretary (West) in the External Affairs Ministry, Sibi George said that during the talks between Prime Minister Modi and the visiting dignitary, there was clear emphasis on 3 Ts – trade, technology and talent.

 

<><><> 

 

Voting is underway across Israel in a high-stakes Parliamentary election, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a strong challenge from former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and other opposition leaders. Over seventy-three lakh thirty one thousand voters are expected to cast their ballots to elect the 26th Knesset, Israel’s parliament.

 

<><><> 

 

India’s Aditya has won the gold medal at the World Under-19 Boxing Championships in Montenegro. Aditya defeated Russia’s Islam Magomedov by a 4-1 margin in the men’s 55-kilogram final to claim the world title.

Meanwhile, Megha Sheokand settled for silver in the women’s 80-kilogram category. Earlier, Harshika won the bronze in the women’s 65-kilogram category, while Prachi Tokas secured a bronze medal in the women’s over-80-kilogram category.

 

<><><> 

 

In Men’s Cricket, India defeated hosts New Zealand by six wickets in the third T-20 International at Wellington today, taking an unassailable three-nil lead in the five-match series. Chasing a target of 199 runs, India stormed to victory in just 13-point-two overs, losing four wickets. Abhishek Sharma led the charge with a sensational 113 off just 38 balls, while his opening partner, Vaibhav Suryavanshi, smashed a quickfire 45 off 19 deliveries.

 

Earlier, New Zealand posted 198 for the loss of three wickets in their stipulated 20 overs.

THE HEADLINES:

  1. Government clears defence procurement for Armed forces worth two lakh 12 thousand crore rupees; 82 per cent of acquisitions to be sourced from Indian Industry.
  2. Cyclone Arnab intensifies over Bay of Bengal; Centre reviews preparedness as Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry brace for impact.
  3. RELIEF scheme for exporters, offering 95 per cent risk cover for shipments, extended till 31st of March amid West Asia crisis.
  4. Usage of 100 per cent ethanol fuel allowed in flex-fuel vehicles as government amends motor vehicle rules.
  5. And, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurates two-day BRICS Parliamentary Forum meeting in New Delhi.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has cleared several capital acquisition proposals for the Armed Forces worth approximately two lakh twelve thousand crore rupees. The Defence Ministry has said, nearly 82 per cent of the procurements will be made from the Indian Industry.

 

 

For the Indian Army, approval has been granted for the procurement of several systems, including High Mobility Vehicles, Self-Propelled Tracked Gun Systems, Light Multi-Role Helicopters, Very Short-Range Air Defence Systems, Surveillance UAVs, Integrated Surveillance and Strike Systems, and Long-Range Kamikaze Drone Systems. More from our correspondent:

 

 

“The High Mobility Vehicles which will be procured for India Army  will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System will provide matching mobility and firepower to mechanised formations. The  Light Multi Role Helicopters will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force for Surveillance, Combat, Search and Rescue of troops, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief among others. For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of Active Offboard Decoy System and other major Naval platforms. This will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles defence, especially against modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries. For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of Helicopters, Air Defence Systems, Weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System to enhance the air defence and war fighting capabilities.  Anand Kumar, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has stressed the need to develop cutting-edge technologies and strengthen supply chains to reduce import dependence and achieve technological superiority in the second phase of self-reliance in the defence sector. Mr Singh was speaking at the fifth edition of the Naval Innovation and Indigenisation Seminar, Swavlamban 2026, in New Delhi today.

 

<><><>

 


Cyclonic Storm Arnab continues to intensify over the Bay of Bengal as it moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, raising concerns over adverse weather in various parts of the country. The evolving weather system is likely to bring heavy rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Southern Odisha, Puducherry, South and Central Chhattisgarh apart from Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

 

 

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said, the storm is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west central Bay of Bengal tonight. It is very likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region tomorrow before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday.

 

 

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparedness measures to tackle the evolving situation. We have a report:

 

 

 

“Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to continuously monitor the cyclone’s movement and take all necessary precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property. District Collectors have been instructed to alert people in vulnerable coastal areas and shift them to cyclone shelters wherever necessary. The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall, with wind speeds likely to reach 115 to 125 kilometres per hour and gusts up to 140 kilometres per hour during landfall. The State Disaster Management Authority has urged people to remain vigilant and follow official advisories. Meanwhile, educational institutions in seven districts have been declared closed on October 27th and 28th as a precautionary measure. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

 

The Odisha government has intensified its preparedness by deploying ministers and rescue teams to coordinate response efforts. Our correspondent has the details:

 

 

 

“Cyclonic Storm Arnab is moving westwards over the Bay of Bengal, about 550 kilometres southeast of Gopalpur in the latest available reports. In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri are under a red warning for Wednesday. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five districts will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday.Railways have cancelled eight trains and curtailed two services as a precaution. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has assigned eight ministers to oversee preparedness in vulnerable districts, while 302 rescue teams have been kept ready.  Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the Bay of Bengal along and off the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Yanam in Puducherry, until Thursday.

 

 

Meanwhile, Cabinet Secretary Dr. TV Somanathan today chaired a meeting of the National Crisis Management Committee to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in the Bay of Bengal. The Chief Secretaries and senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry apprised the Committee of the preparatory measures being undertaken by the State Governments and local administration. Dr. Somanathan stressed the need to ensure zero loss of life, minimise damage to property and infrastructure, and restoration of essential services at the earliest.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Rajasthan government has declared 80 tehsils across 14 districts as drought-affected due to deficient rainfall and damage to kharif crops. Our correspondent has the details:

 

 

“The state government has issued notifications in this regard, taking into account deficient rainfall and damage to Kharif crops. Out of the 80 tehsils, 69 have been classified as severely affected, while 11 have been categorised as moderate affected. The declaration will remain in effect for the next six months. The government’s decision will facilitate the opening of fodder depots for livestock in the affected areas. Recovery of agricultural loans will also remain suspended for six months. Jitendra Dwivedi, Akashvani News, Jaipur.”

 

 

Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel has declared four districts, Kutch, Jamnagar, Porbandar and Devbhoomi Dwarka as drought-affected due to low and delayed rainfall.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Centre has extended the timelines of the Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation (RELIEF) scheme until 31st of March next year, in view of ongoing geopolitical disruptions in West Asia. The initiative aims to encourage exporters to obtain Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India, cover for upcoming shipments to specified regions by providing 95 per cent risk coverage.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The government has allowed the use of E100 ethanol fuel in vehicles specifically designed to run on flexible fuel, under amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways issued a gazette notification in this regard. The decision will pave the path for original equipment manufacturers to launch vehicles engineered to run on 100 percent bio-ethanol fuel.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was taking measures to prevent sudden fluctuations in the value of the rupee. Speaking to reporters at Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu, Ms Sitharaman said India’s fiscal deficit has been declining year after year, with the government working towards reducing the debt-to-GDP ratio to 50 per cent by 2030.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw today flagged off the Jaipur (Khatipura)-Tatanagar-Santragachi Express train. Mr Vaishnaw participated in the programme through video conferencing. Speaking on the occasion, the Minister said, the new train service connecting Jaipur with Jamshedpur and Kolkata will improve rail connectivity between Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Union Food and Consumer Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi today reviewed the availability of essential commodities. He held a discussion with the Secretary and senior officials of the Department of Consumer Affairs in New Delhi on the prevailing price situation, festive-season market trends and stock requirements for the coming year. In a social media post, Mr Joshi noted that adequate buffer stocks of essential commodities are in place, with prices showing signs of stabilisation. 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Union Minister and Senior BJP leader Rajnath Singh has criticized Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge over his alleged remarks on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father.Talking to media, Mr Singh said, the Congress has suffered not just a political downfall but also an ideological decline. Delhi BJP today held a protest near the residence of Congress president over his alleged remarks.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla today inaugurated the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at the historic Samvidhan Sadan in the Parliament House Complex in New Delhi today. The discussions during the two-day meeting is likely to focus on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability, covering AI oversight, emerging technologies and sustainable development.

 

 

Speaking on the occasion, the Lok Sabha Speaker said, Parliaments can play an important role in strengthening mutual understanding and trust, reducing international tensions, and finding peaceful solutions to global challenges. Mr Birla highlighted key challenges, including regional conflicts, wars, economic instability, trade tensions, terrorism and climate change.

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi also attended the inaugural session and met the leaders of the visiting delegations.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has issued orders for placing six officials, including four policemen, under suspension for alleged lapses at a few polling stations of Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency on 23rd of this month. According to an ECI statement, the suspensions were ordered on the basis of an inquiry report filed by the Divisional Commissioner, Agra-cum-Returning Officer for Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency. 

 

 

<><><>

 


In our bilingual live phone-in programme “Public Speak” at 9.30 PM tonight, we will bring a discussion on Public Grievance Portal: Empowering Citizens Through Transparent and Accountable Governance with Sanjeev Saxena, Senior Technical Director, NIC-DARPG.

 

 

 <><><>

 

 

The Indian Olympic Association has announced the contingent for the 2026 Summer Youth Olympic Games set to begin from 31st of this month in Dakar, Senegal. A 17-member athlete contingent including India’s promising young table tennis player Sarthak Arya, will take part in the games across 11 sports. Dakar 2026 marks a historic milestone, as it will be the first Olympic event to be held on the African continent.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Benchmark domestic equity indices rose nearly 0.7 per cent today, snapping a four-session losing streak. The Sensex gained 483 points to close at 73 thousand 607. The Nifty climbed 153 points to settle at 22 thousand 753.

THE HEADLINES:

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi warns against economic warfare, stressing need to shield country’s banking system from cyber terrorism; Inaugurates RBI’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute near Bhubaneswar in Odisha.
  2. Prime Minister Modi in Mann Ki Baat highlights, ‘Vocal for Local’ movement is taking Indian products to global markets.
  3. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar calls upon United Nations to show leadership rather than remaining a spectator to global crises.
  4. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh step up preparedness as deep depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclonic storm by tomorrow.
  5. Saudi Arabia reopens Riyadh airport after two-weeks amid Houthi strikes; Intercepts fresh attacks.
  6. In Women’s Cricket, India set a target of 329 runs for Zimbabwe in second ODI of three-match series in Vadodara.

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stressed the need to protect country’s banking system from cyber terrorism, warning that modern wars are being fought not only through conventional means but also by targeting economies. Mr Modi was speaking after inaugurating the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha, this evening. He said the new facilities will help protect country’s banking system against emerging cyber threats.

 

Mr Modi said India’s banking sector has emerged as one of the most efficient in the world, with people having access to banking services round the clock. Mr Modi said, development means balanced growth across India, creating opportunities for villages and smaller towns alongside major cities.

 

Speaking on the occasion, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said, the new RBI facility will support critical financial infrastructure.

 

Built at an estimated cost of around 170 crore rupees, the data centre is expected to strengthen the security of critical financial data and enhance the resilience of India’s digital financial infrastructure. The accompanying Cybersecurity Training Institute will provide specialised training and promote research in cybersecurity, enterprise computing and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence and quantum computing.

Mr Modi reached Odisha after completing his visit to Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. The Prime Minister attended the third and final day of the mega air show, Wings Over Ganges, at Namo Ghat as the chief guest this morning. The event was organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. We have a report:

 

“People witnessed an extraordinary display of the Indian Air Force’s strength, skill, and valor during the Air Force Day Aerial Display 2026 at NAMO Ghat today. The sky resounded with the roar of combat aircraft such Sukhoi-30MKI, and the Rafale.

 

The high-speed of the Tejas fighter aircraft showcased the strength and capabilities of the Indian Air Force. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army also participated in the aerial display, highlighting the joint operational prowess of India’s armed forces. The ‘Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team’ mesmerized the audience with their daring aerial stunts. Before this Prime Minister Modi inaugurated a new textile manufacturing facility in Varanasi today. Prime Minister also interacted with the female staff there. Prem Chandra gupta, Akashvani News, Varanasi.“

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, ‘Vocal for Local’ movement is helping Indian products reach global markets. He asserted that people are increasingly giving preference to indigenous products during festivals, helping Indian goods reach markets across the world. Mr Modi was addressing the the nation in his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat on Akashvani, marking 12 years of the initiative today.

 

Mr Modi said the growing preference for locally made goods is supporting Indian manufacturers, artisans and small businesses while strengthening the country’s economy. He urged people to prioritise buying products made by local artisans during the upcoming festive season. He said, this will further strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ movement and the dream of ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’.

           

Recalling his visit to IIT Madras in Chennai earlier this month, Mr Modi said the nation’s youth are currently working on subjects that have the potential to transform the future of humanity. He highlighted advances in brain research at IIT Madras. He also spoke about various start-ups he saw which are being supported by the incubation ecosystem at IIT Madras. The Prime Minister said, the supportive ecosystem in the country is helping start-ups develop innovative deep-tech solutions, including application of Artificial Intelligence.

 

<><><> 

 

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar called upon the United Nations to show leadership rather than remaining a spectator to global crises. Dr Jaishankar made the remarks while speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi today. The event marked the 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. The Minister pitched for the world body to recognise its shortcomings and limitations, and seek improvement. The External Affairs Minister said, the need for reformed multilateralism is growing stronger by the day and stressed that large parts of the world cannot be excluded from global decision-making.

 

Dr Jaishankar said, India expresses global sentiment when it urges that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution for global conflicts, stressing that New Delhi is ready to work with international partners towards peace.

 

<><><> 

 

Saudi Arabia has reopened both terminals of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh for domestic and international flights from today, following a suspension of operations for more than two weeks amid deadly strikes by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

Earlier today, Saudi military spokesperson Colonel Turki bin Saleh al-Maliki said the country’s air defence systems intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh before it could reach its target.

Meanwhile, Indian airline IndiGo has announced the cancellation of its flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until the 31st of this month, citing the evolving security situation.

 

<><><> 

 

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said India plans to increase its port capacity four fold by 2047 to support economic growth and expanding international trade. Speaking in Rotterdam during his visit to the Netherlands, Mr Goyal, highlighted opportunities for cooperation with the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands in maritime infrastructure, green energy, carbon capture and sustainable trade. 

 

<><><> 

 

The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will begin in New Delhi tomorrow. The theme of the two day event is – Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations. Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla will preside the over the proceedings.

 

Meanwhile, the Lok Sabha Speaker held bilateral talks with Chairman of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation Vyacheslav Volodin in New Delhi today. The two leaders discussed ways to strengthen India-Russia friendship and parliamentary cooperation.

 

<><><> 

 

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast very heavy rainfall in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh from Tuesday to Thursday in view of the approaching weather system.

Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have stepped up their preparedness measures to deal with the potential impact of the developing cyclone.

The Odisha government has mobilised disaster response teams and stepped up precautionary measures. Our correspondent has the details:

 

“The system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the Wednesday forenoon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour and gusts reaching 140 kilometres per hour. Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri are among the districts facing heightened risks, with a red warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on Wednesday. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has directed the administration to ensure preparedness and minimise casualties. Around 60 ODRAF teams and 17 NDRF teams have been deployed, while 225 Fire Services teams remain on high alert. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five southern districts will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while authorities are preparing for evacuations and possible disruption to transport, power supply and agricultural activities. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

 

Andhra Pradesh is also on high alert as a very severe cyclonic storm is forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. More from our correspondent:

 

“Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has reviewed the state’s preparedness and directed officials to remain alert. Ten NDRF and eleven SDRF teams are ready for rescue operations. Officials are preparing evacuation plans, relief camps, and arrangements for food, drinking water and medical services. Control rooms have been set up in all coastal districts, with helpline numbers made available to the public. The government has directed officials to remove dangerous hoardings. The Electricity Department has kept 25-thousand poles ready for emergency repairs. Hospitals have been directed to provide round-the-clock services. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.“

 

<><><> 

 

The auspicious festival of Sharad Purnima, also known as Lakshmi Puja, is being celebrated across the country with religious fervour and traditional enthusiasm. Devotees are offering special prayers to Goddess Lakshmi, seeking peace, prosperity and well-being for their families. A key ritual of the festival involves preparing kheer, a sweet rice pudding, and placing it in the open sky under the full moon overnight. According to traditional beliefs, the full moon on Sharad Purnima showers nectar-like rays, which are believed to impart special qualities to the offering. By the next morning, the dessert is offered as prasad and shared with family members. For generations, this ritual has has been part of  the festival.

In West Bengal, the festival is being celebrated with devotion across the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions. Among the local Nepali Gorkha community, the occasion is observed as Kojagrat Purnima, with devotees traditionally keeping vigil through the night and offering prayers to Goddess Lakshmi.
